title: Kentucky Chocolate-Pecan Pie
finish: Set chocolate custard, pecans toasted, bourbon in the nose
summary: Pecan pie with chocolate and bourbon. The Kentucky Derby weekend pie — not the trademarked bakery one, the home one.
story: Chocolate and pecans and a little bourbon is what Kentucky puts in a pie shell when the horses are running. It is not the packaged 'Derby' pie from Louisville — that's someone else's name. This is the church-cookbook version: dark chocolate, pecans, bourbon, a custard that slices. Serve barely warm. Whipped cream, not a scoop of ice cream fighting the chocolate.

steps.title: Chocolate
steps.body: Scatter chocolate in the cold crust. It will melt into the custard in the oven.

steps.title: Custard
steps.body: Whisk eggs, sugar, corn syrup, butter, bourbon, vanilla, salt. Pecans. Pour over the chocolate.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 350°F 45–55 minutes until the center is just set. Cool at least 2 hours. Bourbon whipped cream if you are among friends.

proTips.text: The bourbon should be a hello, not a bar fight. Two tablespoons. More and it tastes like you spilled the bottle.

milestones.label: Filled
milestones.hint: Chocolate in the crust, pecans in the custard.

title: Copycat Kern's Derby Pie
finish: Set at the edge, a little wobble in the center, walnuts and chips in every slice
summary: A copycat of Kern's Derby Pie — chocolate chips and walnuts in a flaky crust. Home kitchen, not the bakery box.
story: This is a copycat of Kern's Derby Pie: chocolate chips, chopped walnuts, butter, sugar, eggs, and a little flour so the filling sets like a warm cookie. Bourbon if you want it. Cool it before you cut. Whipped cream on the side. It is a home version of the Louisville classic — not the pie from the bakery.

items: 1 stick (8 Tbsp) unsalted butter, melted and cooled 5 minutes

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.body:
325°F. Put the unbaked crust in a 9-inch pie plate. Crimp the edge.
Set the plate on a sheet pan so if it bubbles over you are not scrubbing the oven.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.body:
In a bowl, whisk the melted butter and sugar until it looks like wet sand.
Whisk in the eggs, one at a time, then vanilla and bourbon if you are using it.
Stir in the flour and salt until no dry streaks.
Fold in the chocolate chips and walnuts.

steps.title: Fill the crust
steps.body:
Pour the filling into the crust. Spread the chips and walnuts so they aren't all in one pile.
Don't overfill — leave a little rim.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body:
325°F for 45–55 minutes.
Done when the edge is set and the center still has a slight jiggle, like gelatin, not soup.
If the crust browns too fast, tent the edge with foil.

steps.title: Cool, then slice
steps.body:
Cool at least 2 hours on a rack. Overnight in the fridge slices cleaner.
Serve at room temp or barely warm. Whipped cream. Not ice cream — this pie is already rich.

proTips.text: Walnuts. Not pecans. That's the whole point of this pie. If you swap pecans you made the other Kentucky pie already in this app.
This is a home pie. If you are selling pies, don't print the bakery's trademark on a box.

milestones.label: Filling mixed
milestones.hint: Butter, sugar, eggs, flour. Chips and walnuts folded in.

milestones.label: Just set
milestones.hint: 325°F, 45–55 min. Slight jiggle in the center.

title: Smoked Barbecue Chicken
summary: A whole bird spatchcocked and halved, rubbed with Ember rub and finished with a sticky Ember sauce glaze. The backyard bird done right.
story: Halves are the working man's chicken — cheaper than breasts, more forgiving than a whole bird, and every piece gets smoke and sauce. Take a whole chicken, spatchcock it, and cut it in half. Season with Ember rub, smoke it steady, and don't sauce too early or the sugar burns before the meat's done. This is Kelly's backyard bird, the one from the grill photo.

items: Ember rub (or your favorite rub), enough to coat
1 cup Ember sauce (or your favorite barbecue sauce), thinned with a splash of apple juice if it's thick

steps.title: Spatchcock and halve
steps.body: Cut out the backbone, press the breast flat, then cut the bird in half through the breastbone. Pat dry. Season all over with Ember rub — under the skin where you can reach.

steps.title: Smoke
steps.body: Pit at 275–300°F with hickory or apple, skin-side up. About 2 to 2½ hours.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.body: When the thighs read 165°F, brush on the Ember sauce. Give it 20–30 more minutes so the glaze sets and gets sticky.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.body: Pull at 175°F in the thigh (breast 160°F). Rest 10 minutes, then cut each half into leg and breast portions.

proTips.text: Sauce late. Sugar burns — the glaze goes on in the last half hour, not the first.
Halves over direct heat for the last 5 minutes if you want the skin to bite through.
